name: Coinbase BTC/USD Kyle lambda price-impact drift
description: Over a rolling window of the last window_trades (N) Coinbase BTC/USD trades, kyle_lambda = sum(mid_change_i * signed_volume_i) / sum(signed_volume_i^2): the least-squares slope through the origin of per-trade midpoint change on signed volume, a form chosen for the exact-decimal idiom because it needs only multiply and divide. Each trade's signed_volume_i (trade size times aggressor sign, positive for a buyer-aggressor) pairs with the Coinbase midpoint change that FOLLOWS it — from the midpoint prevailing at the trade to the next observed Coinbase midpoint update — so the estimator measures price impact rather than anticipation; trades between two midpoint updates share that same forward change, and a trade with no subsequent midpoint update yet has no completed pair. lambda_drift is the current window's lambda minus the previous disjoint window's lambda. Fewer than 2N completed pairs, or a window whose sum of squared signed volume is zero, is a defined not-ready state and never a division by zero. window_trades defaults to 100. This identity is single-venue by construction: the measurement compares one venue's own trades and book against each other, so it reads only Coinbase inputs and is ready whenever the Coinbase book-and-trade join is fresh, independently of the other adopted spot venue. No blended `btc.external.*` variant of this measurement is published: a cross-venue form would have to rule which venue's book prices another venue's trade, and that ruling is deferred pending evidence (ADR 0023 amendment and ADR 0024, both 2026-09-02). Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
